title: Classification of planar monomials in odd characteristic
summary: Determine whether the known Dembowski-Ostrom and characteristic-three Coulter-Matthews families exhaust all planar monomials up to graph equivalence.

formal_statement.body: For every odd prime $p$, positive integer $n$, and exponent $d$, suppose $x\mapsto x^d$ is perfect nonlinear, equivalently planar, on $\mathbb F_{p^n}$. Prove that it is graph-equivalent to a known Dembowski-Ostrom planar monomial or, when $p=3$, to a Coulter-Matthews monomial, or exhibit a planar monomial outside these graph-equivalence classes.

scope.domain: Perfect nonlinear power functions over finite fields of odd characteristic
assumptions: The function is the monomial $x^d$ on $\mathbb F_{p^n}$
Classification is taken up to graph equivalence
scope.unresolved_remainder: The conjecture has been computationally verified for fields of order at most 2^30, and the p>5 cases with extension degree n a power of two are classified. The complete all-characteristic, all-extension-degree classification remains open outside the known strict subranges.

provenance.note: Zieve's 2013 primary text calls the full classification a folk conjecture, so neither it nor the 2020 TIT restatement establishes the original proposer.

citations.label: Beierle--Beyne, degree bound for planar functions

progress.summary: Zieve describes the exhaustion of the known planar monomial families as a folk conjecture and proves a large-field fixed-degree result.
The TIT source restates the conjecture that the listed families exhaust the perfect-nonlinear power functions.
A public preprint computationally verifies the classification for every finite field of order at most 2^30.
A published degree-bound result completes the classification for p>5 when the extension degree is a power of two and leaves the general classification open.
